title: Rockingham County family pleads for answers nearly 2 months after deadly hit-and-run: 'Why not say something?' - NewsBreak
text:
By Tiana Maxwell ,
1 hours ago ROCKINGHAM COUNTY, N.C. (WGHP) -- A Rockingham County family wants answers after their loved one was hit and killed by a driver on Father's Day.
Jenny Damian said that relaying the story of how her uncle Javier Hernandez Sandoval's last moments alive happened to family members is a devastating story to tell.
Rockingham County family pleads for answers nearly 2 months after deadly hit-and-run (WGHP) The North Carolina Highway Patrol identified the 65-year-old as the victim of a fatal hit-and-run in June. Troopers responded to the area of NC 65 and NC 87 near the Rockingham County Courthouse on June 21.
"My son would say, ... 'Where's uncle? Where's uncle?' You know? My son is only 8 years old," Damian said.
Damian said her uncle often chose walking as his way to get around town. She said he was walking that night to visit a nearby grocery store when the unthinkable happened.
Investigators have not identified a suspect in the case. A lieutenant said the case is open and active. Investigators said the suspected vehicle is gray or silver in color with front-end damage.
Damian said her family is angry and frustrated that they have no answers to their questions after several weeks have passed.
"Put yourself in my situation," Damien said. "What would you do? If you knew what was going on, if you knew who it was, why not report it? Why not say something?"
She said they searched for answers on their own by retracing their loved one's footsteps.
"My daughter and I walked out there looking for any, and we can't find anything, but something has to come up," Damian said. "How do you not see something? ... Almost two months, and we still don't have any kind of answers to what is going on."
She has a message for anyone who sees a vehicle that matches the investigator's description.
"If you see that, just call it in," Damian said. "Maybe it's not anything, but what if it is? I know they have been looking into a lot of vehicles, but we still haven't been able to get any answers."
The family is working to return Sandoval Hernandez's ashes to his wife and children in Mexico.
Damian said they plan on accompanying their loved one on the journey. She said that sending him alone, similarly to how the suspected driver left him on the road, would be unacceptable.
"We love him that much, and we want to keep him with the family," Damian said. "We enjoyed the last 30-something years. ... Now, he can rest easy with his family."
They plan to make the journey in the next few weeks.
Anyone with information is asked to call the NCSHP at (336) 634-5606 during business hours or dial *HP(47) anytime.
